rayTracing.title: Ray Tracing Channel Generation for 6G
rayTracing.imageAlt: Illustration of a rooftop antenna emitting glowing signal rays across stylized city buildings toward a mobile receiver
rayTracing.pitch: A methodology for generating physically accurate 6G channel data with ray tracing — a real street in Fortaleza, a real base-station position, and moving vehicles and pedestrians, instead of a statistical channel model.

sudoku.title: Sudoku Assistant Pro
sudoku.imageAlt: Screenshot of a Sudoku grid with pencil-mark candidate numbers in the Sudoku Assistant Qt desktop app
sudoku.pitch: A native Sudoku solver and player built with Qt6 and C++17, following strict MVP architecture — pencil-mark candidates are painted directly onto cells through a custom delegate instead of nested widgets, and the UI switches between English and French at runtime.

tortoise.title: Tortoise World
tortoise.imageAlt: Top-down grid game screenshot showing a tortoise agent, lettuce, water and rocks scattered across a yellow arena, with a dog roaming nearby
tortoise.pitch: A rational agent that has to eat every lettuce in an N×N grid while staying alive — A* search with a cost function that repels it from a roaming dog, and a priority-based finite state machine that decides when to interrupt the hunt to drink.

about: Hi, I'm Abraão — a Dual Degree Engineering student between Universidade Federal do Ceará (Brazil) and Ensicaen (France).
I specialize in Cybersecurity & E-payment, and I like building secure, efficient full-stack applications.
Currently working with React, Next.js, TypeScript and Python — see what I'm building in the Projects section below.

chamberOrchestra.imageAlt: Illustration of a central AI orchestrator agent connected to smaller agent and music-note nodes
chamberOrchestra.pitch: An AI agent orchestration framework that turns a Jira ticket straight into a reviewed Merge Request — no human coding in between.

agents.imageAlt: Diagram of the seven-agent pipeline, from blueprint to shipped Merge Request
lines: An Architect drafts the blueprint, a Developer implements it, then an Inspector and a Remediation Developer audit and patch it.
Styles, Localization and Release Manager agents close the loop — styling, translations, and the Merge Request itself.
Project files are chunked, embedded and stored in a ChromaDB vector database.
Agents pull the most relevant code via semantic search, kept in sync by a job that also garbage-collects deleted files.

results.imageAlt: Mockup of the Device Manager dashboard showing device status cards
lines: Device Manager is live in production, replacing a manual reservation workflow.
13 tickets processed end-to-end — some merge requests needed zero human intervention.
Jira fires a signed webhook the moment a ticket moves to In Progress.
A FastAPI middleware verifies the SHA-256 signature and queues the workflow asynchronously, so Jira never times out.

boJogar.title: BóJogar
boJogar.imageAlt: Screenshot of the BóJogar iOS app's home feed listing a user's sports events
boJogar.meta: iOS App + API @ Apple Developer Academy
boJogar.pitch: A sports-events app for people who just moved somewhere new — a feed of nearby games to join, and the tools to create and run your own. The SwiftUI app and its Node.js API, built end-to-end.

lines: Maria just moved to a new city. She loves sports, but knows no one and has no idea where locals play.
No listing of nearby courts, tracks or fields, and no easy way to find people who share her sport.
People like Maria: newcomers looking for a way back into their sport.
Regular pickup groups, public agencies opening community events, and local businesses after more visibility.
A feed of sports events near the user, with one tap to create and manage their own.
Each event keeps its own participant list, from open pickup games to organized tournaments.

images: The BóJogar home screen listing a user's created and joined sports events
The events screen listing active sports events nearby, with a search bar
An event's detail screen showing its location, time and list of participants
The locations screen showing sports venues on a map with their scheduled events

seelect.title: SEELECT
seelect.pitch: As logistics coordinator for a 200+ person academic week, I built the registration platform — a full-stack app to handle sign-ups, payments and live attendance, run day-to-day by a 10-person team.

lines: A React frontend talks to a Django REST API that handles secure participant authentication and registration.
Payment for registration fees happens directly in the sign-up flow — no cash, no spreadsheet tracking by hand.
The event ran on a student budget with no money purpose, so paid cloud hosting was off the table.
We self-hosted the Django backend on our own local infrastructure to keep it 100% free.
During the event, the same platform tracked attendance in real time as the team checked participants into each session.
Presence data doubled as the source of truth for who'd earned a certificate.
checkin.imageAlt: Illustration of a central check-in node connected to a grid of participant nodes, some lit to show attendance

lines: At the end of the week, a script auto-generates a completion certificate for each of the 200+ participants.
What used to take hours of manual work now runs in minutes.
certificates.imageAlt: Illustration of a hub emitting certificate-shaped document icons in a grid
